This exporter writes logs to Amazon S3. Unlike the upstream
[`awss3exporter`](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/tree/main/exporter/awss3exporter),
the destination is not fixed at startup: each event carries its own S3 routing
information (bucket, region, role to assume and payload format) in its
attributes. This makes the exporter suitable for a dynamic, multi-tenant
topology where different events are destined for different buckets owned by
different AWS accounts.

It is designed for the Elastic Streams S3 destination described in the
[S3 Destination RFC](https://github.com/elastic/ingest-dev/issues/8340).

## How it works

- **Per-event routing.** For every log record the exporter reads the configured
  routing attributes (first from the log record, then falling back to resource
  attributes). Records are grouped by their resolved destination and one S3
  object is written per destination.
- **Tenant identity from context.** The tenant a batch belongs to (a hosted
  deployment or a serverless project, plus its org) is not read from event
  attributes. The deployment/project ID and its type come once per call from
  the request's client metadata (the `X-Elastic-Target-Id` /
  `X-Elastic-Target-Type` headers, as stamped by upstream pipeline
  components); the org ID still comes from the `org_id` attribute. A batch
  arriving without that context is dropped in full, since there is no
  identity to authenticate the upload with.
- **Web identity role assumption.** Authentication uses STS
  `AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity`. For each tenant the exporter fetches a
  short-lived web identity (JWT) token from a local token endpoint and
  exchanges it, together with the event's `role_arn`, for temporary
  credentials scoped to the destination. This enables cross-account writes
  without long-lived credentials. Credentials are wrapped in an
  `aws.CredentialsCache` and refreshed automatically.
- **mTLS identity, not a self-declared header.** The exporter never builds an
  `X-Forwarded-Client-Cert` header itself. Instead, per tenant, it generates a
  self-signed client certificate whose DNS Subject Alternative Name encodes
  the tenant's identity (`<deploymentID>.deployment.<orgID>.account` for
  hosted, `EIDENT.<projectID>.project.observability.type.<orgID>.organization`
  for serverless) and presents it on the mTLS connection to the token
  endpoint. In production the token endpoint must be reached through the ECP
  proxy — never the workload-identity-issuer service directly — since the
  proxy is what terminates that connection, verifies the certificate, and
  derives the XFCC header itself from the SAN it observed on the wire.
- **Token caching & refresh.** Tokens are fetched once per tenant and cached
  until `refresh_skew` before their `expires_at`, then refetched. If STS rejects
  a token (`ExpiredTokenException`, `InvalidIdentityToken`, `IDPRejectedClaim`),
  the cached token is invalidated and a fresh one is fetched on the next
  attempt. The identity certificate itself is regenerated independently once
  it is within `refresh_skew` of `cert_ttl`.
- **Client caching.** Instantiating an S3 client and assuming a role on every
  event would be expensive. The exporter keeps a bounded in-memory LRU cache of
  S3 clients keyed by `(target_type, target_id, org_id, role_arn, region,
  bucket)`. On a cache hit the cached client is reused; on a miss a new client
  is created and cached.
- **Object naming.** Objects are named deterministically to avoid collisions:
  `logs/<tenant_id>/YYYY/MM/DD/HH/<uuid>.<ext>` (UTC). The extension depends on
  the resolved format (`json` for OTLP JSON, `binpb` for OTLP protobuf).
- **Reliability.** The standard exporter `sending_queue`, `retry_on_failure` and
  `timeout` settings apply. Records missing required routing attributes or
  requesting an unsupported format are dropped (permanent failures); only
  upload errors, which may be transient, are surfaced to the retry machinery.

## Configuration

```yaml
exporters:
  awss3:
    # Attribute keys that carry per-event routing information. Defaults shown.
    # The tenant's target type/ID come from request context, not attributes;
    # see "Authentication" below.
    attributes:
      bucket: bucket          # required attribute: destination bucket name
      role_arn: role_arn      # required attribute: IAM role ARN to assume
      region: region          # required attribute: destination bucket region
      org_id: org_id          # required attribute: tenant org ID (token scope)
      format: format          # optional attribute: payload format
      tenant_id: tenant_id    # optional attribute: used in the object key

    # Payload format used when a record does not carry the format attribute.
    # Supported: otlp_json (aliases: json, ""), otlp_proto (aliases: proto,
    # protobuf, otlp_protobuf).
    default_format: otlp_json

    # Local endpoint that mints per-tenant web identity tokens for
    # AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity. In production this must be the ECP proxy, not
    # the workload-identity-issuer service directly (see "Authentication").
    token_endpoint:
      url: http://localhost:8443/token  # mTLS-authenticated POST
      region: ""                         # sent as the X-Elastic-Region header
      audience: sts.amazonaws.com        # sent in the request body ("aud")
      refresh_skew: 5m                   # refetch this long before expires_at
      timeout: 10s                       # per-request HTTP timeout
      cert_ttl: 24h                      # validity window of the generated identity certificate

    # Shared knobs applied to every AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity call. The role ARN
    # itself is taken per-event from the role_arn attribute.
    sts:
      session_name: elastic-streams-s3-exporter
      region: ""            # STS client region (default: SDK resolution)

    # Bounded LRU cache of assumed-role S3 clients.
    client_cache:
      size: 128             # max cached (target_type, target_id, org_id, role_arn, region, bucket) clients

    # For S3-compatible stores / tests only.
    endpoint: ""
    disable_ssl: false
    s3_force_path_style: false

    # Standard exporterhelper settings.
    sending_queue:
    retry_on_failure:
    timeout: 5s
```

### Authentication

Authentication uses IAM role assumption via STS `AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity`,
with the tenant's identity conveyed via mTLS rather than a self-declared
header:

- The tenant's target type (`hosted` or `serverless`) and target ID
  (deployment ID or project ID) are resolved once per export call from the
  request's client metadata — the `X-Elastic-Target-Type` /
  `X-Elastic-Target-Id` headers, as stamped by upstream pipeline components —
  not from event attributes. The org ID still comes from the `org_id`
  attribute.
- For each distinct `(target_type, target_id, org_id)` the exporter generates
  a self-signed client certificate whose only DNS SAN encodes that identity:
  - hosted: `<deploymentID>.deployment.<orgID>.account`
  - serverless: `EIDENT.<projectID>.project.observability.type.<orgID>.organization`
- The exporter POSTs to the configured `token_endpoint.url` over a TLS
  connection presenting that certificate, plus the `X-Elastic-Region` header
  and a body of `{"aud":"<audience>"}`. It never sets an
  `X-Forwarded-Client-Cert` header itself. In production `token_endpoint.url`
  must point at the ECP proxy: the proxy terminates the mTLS connection,
  verifies the certificate, and builds the XFCC header from the SAN it
  observed — the workload-identity-issuer trusts that header only because the
  proxy, not the caller, produced it. The endpoint returns
  `{"token": "<jwt>", "expires_at": <unix-seconds>}`.
- The returned JWT is exchanged, together with the event's `role_arn`, for
  temporary credentials via `AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity`. The `role_arn`'s trust
  policy must permit the web identity provider/audience.
- Tokens are cached per tenant until `refresh_skew` before `expires_at` and
  refetched on expiry. If STS rejects a token as expired/invalid, it is
  refetched on the next attempt. The identity certificate is regenerated
  independently once it is within `refresh_skew` of `cert_ttl`.
- Temporary credentials obtained via STS are reused via `aws.NewCredentialsCache`.
